title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev
talk_summary: Bergum argues BM25 lexical retrieval is newly effective for agents because the LLM is a 'more powerful user' that writes long, operator-rich queries and can inspect literal matches to reformulate. He shows retrieval quality dominates end-to-end accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus, that BM25 parameter choice matters a lot, and that exposing retrieved docs as a filesystem workspace lets agents use grep/bash-style progressive disclosure.

takeaways.what_they_do: Retriever results are placed into a virtual file system workspace with title + snippet exposed first; the agent reads more via normal file/bash tools (progressive disclosure).
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you organize this workspace as a file system, you can ... have progressive disclosure because you can have the document like the title of the document and a small snippet

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a cheap BM25 search tool returning snippets; combine with grep because both reward literal term matching the model can reason about.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the combination of these two is a very strong agentic search or agentic retrieval paradigm

takeaways.technique: Task-level eval, not single-query retrieval metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues classical one-query NDCG evaluation is obsolete for agents; measure whether the agent completes the task (e.g., exact answer) across its multi-query trajectory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of the classical information retrieval evaluation is now kind of dead ... see if the model can perform the task

takeaways.technique: Tune retrieval/scoring params, don't trust defaults
takeaways.what_they_do: Shows the BrowseComp-Plus BM25 baseline was 'terrible' because its hyperparameters didn't fit long documents; re-tuning changed benchmark accuracy dramatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the parameters that were used in the browse comp plus research paper was not really adequate to handle these kind of long documents

takeaways.what_they_do: Prefers BM25 over embedding infra because exact matches (names, SKUs, IDs) are hard for embeddings and BM25 avoids embedding-inference cost and infra.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's also relatively cheap especially if you take into consideration the cost of doing embedding inference
